notes: The complete named schema surface is represented over the primitive Coq modal syntax.
Primitive syntax, derived connectives, substitution, complexity, degree, subformula closure, and a surjective enumeration over nat atoms are checked; upstream generic convenience APIs remain.
Syntactic complement and complement-closed finite contexts are checked; Hilbert derivability lemmas await the entailment layer.

NNF syntax, decidable equality, structural negation, translations, degree, modal CNF/DNF predicates, and a surjective enumeration over nat atoms are checked; Lean-specific generic encoding instances remain.
The concrete modal connectives and boxdot operation are represented; upstream abstract connective typeclasses remain.
Formula-indexed frames/models, full satisfaction algebra, validity and countermodel equivalences, sound structural rules, and failure of replacement of equivalents are checked.

The concrete K Lindenbaum chain, finite-stage localization, consistency preservation, and maximal completion are checked in a one-sided presentation; the upstream generic two-sided tableau convenience API remains.

Concrete maximal consistent K theories, Lindenbaum extension, derivability closure, negation and implication membership, and the modal successor lemma are checked; upstream generic named-system and list-connective API remains.
The concrete normal calculus K, substitution, derived classical rules, predicate theories, deduction, consistency criteria, and contextual boxing are checked; arbitrary named-axiom extensions remain.
The general semantic correspondence and named instances are checked; canonical-frame instances await the Hilbert layer.
Weak n-transitivity, its exact Geach characterization, arbitrary-formula validity, and the atomic converse are checked; the generic canonical-frame instance awaits named Hilbert systems.

The exact Grz correspondence with reflexivity, transitivity, and weak converse well-foundedness is checked, including the irreflexive-reduction characterization; finite-frame convenience instances remain.
Detour-freedom and no-proper-detour are characterized, imply antisymmetry, and exactly correspond to atomic H validity; generated-frame and canonical instances remain.
The Boolos frame condition and its transitive-frame validity theorem are checked for arbitrary formulas.
The exact atomic frame correspondence is checked; finite-frame convenience instances remain.
The McKinsey frame condition and arbitrary-formula validity theorem are checked; the extended-Hilbert derivations and canonical instance remain.
The Makinson frame condition and arbitrary-formula Mk validity theorem are checked; the canonical theorem, which contains an upstream sorry at the pin, remains.
The exact semantic correspondence is checked; canonical-frame connectedness awaits the Hilbert layer.
The Sobocinski condition, its structural consequences, arbitrary-formula validity, and exact atomic converse are checked; the canonical-frame instance remains.
Isolation is shown exactly equivalent to atomic Ver validity; the named-system canonical instance remains.
Piecewise convergence is shown exactly equivalent to atomic WeakPoint2 validity, with arbitrary-formula and strong-to-weak corollaries; the named-system canonical instance remains.
Piecewise connectedness, its distinct-successor characterization, and its exact atomic WeakPoint3 correspondence are checked; the named-system canonical instance remains.
Antisymmetry, strict/pre/partial orders, and closure preservation are checked; Lean-only inherited instances are unnecessary in the Coq representation.
Asymmetry is characterized by irreflexivity plus antisymmetry, including the transitive specialization.
Core frames, models, validity, iteration, substitution, and K validity are checked; upstream generated-model and frame-class utilities remain.
Reflexive, positive, and reflexive-transitive closures and their exact algebraic and frame-property preservation theorems are checked.
The bounded generated frame/model, budgeted subformula truth lemma, root truth theorem, and target-invariance theorem are checked generically over atom types.
The canonical K frame/model, modal successor existence, truth lemma, countermodel theorem, and completeness are checked; upstream generic named-system and iterated relation characterizations remain.
Coarsest, finest, and transitive-closure filtrations, truth lemmas, finite bounds, and elementary preservation are checked; rooted confluence/connectedness preservation remains.
K theoremhood and contextual derivability are Kripke-sound on every frame, and consistency is checked; arbitrary axiom-set and frame-class instances remain.
Irreflexivity and its closure/order relationships are checked constructively.
Soundness, consistency, canonical completeness, and finite-frame completeness of concrete Hilbert K are independently checked.
Direct NNF semantics, classical negation, both syntax translations, model/frame validity equivalences, and semantic round trips are checked generically over atom types.
Bisimulation invariance and bounded-morphism truth/validity preservation are checked; closure and injectivity utilities remain.

Roots, generated frames/models, inherited relation properties, bounded morphisms, truth invariance, and positive-reachability generation are checked; the source finiteness typeclass instance is representation-only because local frames carry no finiteness witness.
Target termination, direct termination on transitive frames, closure invariance, converse-well-founded consequences, and target terminality are checked.
The two-cycle-to-singleton bounded-morphism proof of irreflexivity undefinability is checked constructively.
A deep translation for the full primitive modal syntax and arbitrary atom types strengthens the upstream NNFormula/nat statement.
